statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-132138: the cyrus-sasl SCRAM server plugin dereferences a NULL channel-binding pointer in scram_server_mech_step2 when a client sends channel-binding data that the server application did not register, crashing the server (https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-132138, https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2576234). The fix is upstream commit 45d66335a4a6a59ef07b6fe8f94ac843c1fd3b86 (https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/commit/45d66335a4a6a59ef07b6fe8f94ac843c1fd3b86), which adds a "sparams->cbinding == NULL" check that fails with "Server does not support channel binding type received in %s" before the strcmp. That commit is on the master branch; the identical change was also committed to the release branch as d0f9021eccb9dc2f49006d3d3dffe9aaab44dd05 (https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/commit/d0f9021eccb9dc2f49006d3d3dffe9aaab44dd05), which is in the history of the cyrus-sasl-2.1.28 tag. So cyrus-sasl 2.1.28 carries the check in plugins/scram.c (https://github.com/cyrusimap/cyrus-sasl/blob/cyrus-sasl-2.1.28/plugins/scram.c#L1284) and 2.1.27 does not, and in 2.1.28 every server-side dereference of sparams->cbinding comes after it. Red Hat's tracking bug also states the fix was released in cyrus-sasl 2.1.28. The DHI Debian repository now publishes one cyrus-sasl2 build for Debian 13, 2.1.28+dfsg1-9+deb13u0+dhi2, a rebuild of Debian 2.1.28+dfsg1-9 whose only DHI patch removes the SRP plugin and does not touch plugins/scram.c. In that build, on amd64 and arm64, both places the SCRAM server code ships contain the "Server does not support channel binding type received" error string, which only the added check emits: the plugin libscram.so.2.0.25 in libsasl2-modules and the static library libsasl2.a in libsasl2-dev, each package verified against the index checksum. This replaces an earlier assessment whose range ended at an old-scheme build that sorts above the current one. The range ends at 2.1.28+dfsg1-9+deb13u0+dhi2, the first and only published build in the current DHI Debian version scheme.
